references.text: The youngest son squandered all he had in a wild lifestyle, which the older brother accuses him of here. See [ref:Luk 15:13|Luke 15:13].
Proverbs warns against wasting wealth on prostitutes, which the older brother accuses the younger of doing: [ref:Ordsp 29:3|Proverbs 29:3].
A warning that strangers may be filled from your wealth – parallel to the accusation of having consumed the father's property with prostitutes: [ref:Ordsp 5:10|Proverbs 5:10].
The law concerning the rebellious son who is a glutton and a drunkard parallels the older brother's description of the younger: [ref:5 Mos 21:20|Deuteronomy 21:20].
The father ordered the fattened calf to be slaughtered when the youngest returned home – this is the action the older brother complains about: [ref:Luk 15:23|Luke 15:23].
The older brother's complaint in this verse contrasts with his own claim of faithful service, noting he never even received a young goat: [ref:Luk 15:29|Luke 15:29].
The Pharisees complained that Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners – the older brother's attitude reflects this objection: [ref:Luk 5:30|Luke 5:30].
A warning that a prostitute can reduce a man to a mere crust of bread – parallel to the accusation of having consumed his wealth with prostitutes: [ref:Ordsp 6:26|Proverbs 6:26].
The Pharisees and scribes grumbled because Jesus welcomed sinners, which sets the context for the entire parable and explains the older brother's bitterness: [ref:Luk 15:2|Luke 15:2].
